entries.name: OCW2 clear rotate AEOI
entries.description: OCW2 with rotate, specific and end-of-interrupt bits all clear: clears rotation in automatic EOI mode.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 0 and bits 4 and 3 are 0; bits 2 to 0 are ignored. MAME resets the priority order so IR0 is the highest.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X clears its rotate-on-auto-EOI flag instead and keeps no priority order.

entries.name: OCW3
entries.description: OCW3: selects which register a read of the status port returns and starts a poll.
entries.behaviour: Bit 3 set with bits 4 and 7 clear marks it; this is the form with bits 6 and 5 clear. Bit 1 set makes bit 0 the register a read returns (0 request, 1 in-service); bit 2 starts a poll.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X does not handle the poll command; MAME does.

entries.name: OCW3 special mask off
entries.description: OCW3 with bits 6 and 5 equal to 10: leaves special mask mode.
entries.behaviour: Bit 6 enables the special mask change and bit 5 clear resets it; bits 2 to 0 act as in the plain OCW3. MAME only stores bit 5, which its source marks as a TODO.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X acts on special mask mode; MAME stores the bit only.

entries.name: OCW3 special mask on
entries.description: OCW3 with bits 6 and 5 equal to 11: enters special mask mode.
entries.behaviour: Bit 6 enables the special mask change and bit 5 set sets it; bits 2 to 0 act as in the plain OCW3. MAME only stores bit 5, which its source marks as a TODO.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X acts on special mask mode; MAME stores the bit only.

entries.name: ICW1
entries.description: ICW1: starts the initialization sequence and resets the controller.
entries.behaviour: Bit 4 set marks it; bits 7 to 5 are address bits for 8080 mode and are not keyed. Bit 3 selects level-triggered mode, bit 2 an interval of 4, bit 1 single and bit 0 that ICW4 follows. It clears the mask and in-service registers.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X logs level-triggered mode, the interval of 4 and 8080 mode as not handled; MAME keeps the level-triggered flag.

sources.cites: b. The Interrupt Mask Register is cleared.

entries.name: non-specific EOI
entries.description: OCW2 non-specific end of interrupt: the highest-priority in-service interrupt is finished.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 001 and bits 4 and 3 are 0; bits 2 to 0 are ignored. It clears the highest-priority bit set in the in-service register.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X clears the bit of the IRQ it has active and ignores the command when none is; MAME clears the first in-service bit from the priority base.

entries.name: OCW2 no operation
entries.description: OCW2 with bits 7 to 5 equal to 010: no operation.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 010 and bits 4 and 3 are 0. Nothing changes.

entries.name: specific EOI
entries.description: OCW2 specific end of interrupt: the in-service bit of the level in bits 2 to 0 is cleared.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 011 and bits 4 and 3 are 0. Bits 2 to 0 name the interrupt level whose in-service bit is cleared.

entries.name: OCW2 set rotate AEOI
entries.description: OCW2 with bits 7 to 5 equal to 100: rotate in automatic EOI mode, set.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 100 and bits 4 and 3 are 0; bits 2 to 0 are ignored. MAME advances the lowest priority by one on the write.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X sets a rotate-on-auto-EOI flag and does not rotate.

entries.name: rotate on non-spec. EOI
entries.description: OCW2 rotate on non-specific EOI: the in-service interrupt is finished and becomes the lowest priority.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 101 and bits 4 and 3 are 0; bits 2 to 0 are ignored. MAME clears the first in-service bit from the priority base and rotates the base past it.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X logs that rotation is not supported and performs a plain non-specific EOI.

entries.name: set priority
entries.description: OCW2 set priority: the level in bits 2 to 0 becomes the lowest priority.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 110 and bits 4 and 3 are 0. Bits 2 to 0 name the bottom-priority level, so the next level becomes the highest.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X logs that the command is not handled and changes nothing.

entries.name: rotate on specific EOI
entries.description: OCW2 rotate on specific EOI: the in-service bit of the level in bits 2 to 0 is cleared and that level becomes the lowest priority.
entries.behaviour: Chosen when bits 7 to 5 are 111 and bits 4 and 3 are 0. Bits 2 to 0 name the level; MAME clears its in-service bit if set and rotates the priority base past it.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X logs that rotation is not supported, then takes its specific-EOI path.
